Arunachala

A Pilgrimage to Arunachala: The Mountain of Silence
21 – 28 January 2027 · 7 days · 6 nights
With Mitch Hunter & Rose Lamont
Strictly limited to 16 places

Tiruvannamalai is one of the most sacred sites in South India — a living pilgrimage town at the foot of the holy mountain of Arunachala, long associated with the sage Ramana Maharshi. This seven-day retreat is an opportunity to go deep: to meditate in the caves where Ramana lived in silence, sit with living teachers, walk the ancient mountain path by full moon, and spend uninterrupted time in your own practice.

We stay in a beautifully crafted property on the outskirts of Tiruvannamalai — a space of dark timber, raw stone, open courtyards and tropical gardens, with direct views of the mountain.

This is an intimate, practice-based retreat — limited to sixteen sincere practitioners — held in the place long considered the spiritual heart of the world.

Arunachala
The Power of Arunachala

"Aruna, which means 'red, bright like fire', does not signify the mere fire that gives off heat. Rather, it means Jnanagni, the Fire of Wisdom, which is neither hot nor cold. Achala signifies hill. Thus, Arunachala means the Hill of Wisdom."

Arunachaleswarar Temple
One of the great temples of South India,
at the very foot of the mountain
The living lineage

In the presence of Ramana Maharshi

For more than a century, seekers from across the world have been drawn to the foot of Arunachala by the sage Ramana Maharshi — who pointed, again and again, to the single question: Who am I? His ashram still sits at the base of the mountain, a place of silence and quiet devotion.

We sit in the hall where he lived and taught, climb to the caves where he spent years in silence, and spend time in the presence of those still holding this lineage today.

The days

How we'll spend our days

Each day moves between practice, sacred exploration, and rest. The rhythm is intentional but not rigid — there is space to breathe, to go inward, and to find your own pace.

  • Ramana Maharshi's Ashram — sitting in the hall where he lived and taught
  • Virupaksha Cave — where Ramana spent years in silent meditation on the mountain
  • Skandashram — his hillside retreat, with wide views across the plains
  • Annamalai Swami's Ashram — a place of great simplicity, close to the mountain
  • Time with living saints — an opportunity to sit in the presence of those still holding this lineage
  • Morning yoga and meditation
  • Evening meditation & Satsang with Mitch
  • One-on-one sessions with Mitch — personal time to deepen your practice and work through what is arising
  • Authentic homemade Indian cuisine — sattvic, purely vegetarian, prepared fresh daily
  • Unstructured time — to rest, journal, swim, walk, or sit with your own practice

22 January · Purnima

Full Moon GirivalamWalking the mountain through the night

The 22nd of January is Purnima — the full moon. On this night, up to 500,000 pilgrims walk Girivalam: the ancient 14km circumambulation of Arunachala, stopping at each of the eight lingams. We join the walk during the most sacred hours of the night.

There are two options: a shorter 1–2km section, or the full 14km route (4–6 hours). Once on the route it is not possible to turn back, and no vehicles are permitted on the pilgrim path.

Your guides

Teachers

Meditation & Inner Practice

Mitch Hunter

Mitch Hunter is a mystic, meditation teacher, and former academic in the School of Physiotherapy at Griffith University. His work is grounded in the spiritual tradition of Sri Ramana Maharshi and Advaita Vedanta.

He has over twenty-five years of meditation practice and a lifelong history of mystical experiences that culminated in a stabilised awakening in 2019. Since then a silent and causeless joy has remained within him, guiding both his life and his teaching.

This awakening reshaped his approach to physiotherapy, teaching, and the way he supports others. Mitch now works full-time helping people turn inward to recognise their true nature and move toward self-realisation. His work blends jnana yoga with modern health sciences to offer a direct and accessible path to inner healing and meaningful transformation — for individuals and the wider collective.

Yoga, Meditation & Philosophy

Rose Lamont

Rose Lamont is a yoga and meditation teacher, writer and filmmaker based in Australia. She has been teaching yoga, meditation and philosophy for more than a decade and is the co-founder of Ritual Studios, established in 2015.

Her teaching is informed by the study and practice of Raja Yoga, Hatha Yoga, Vipassana meditation, and contemporary postural traditions including Iyengar and Katonah Yoga. Alongside her work as a teacher, Rose facilitates yoga teacher trainings, retreats and specialised courses in philosophy, meditation and pranayama.

With a background in law and philosophy, Rose's work explores the intersection of consciousness, culture, spirituality and the enduring human search for meaning. She is the host of the Wisdom Now podcast and director of a forthcoming documentary on the life and teachings of her mentor, Rose Baudin.

Through teaching, writing, filmmaking and conversation, Rose is interested in how ancient wisdom traditions can illuminate contemporary life. Her work is grounded in a commitment to sincere practice, ongoing study, inquiry, and the direct experience of yoga as a living tradition.

The home

Where we stay

Our accommodation sits a few kilometres outside Tiruvannamalai, with direct sightlines to the mountain. Stone cottages with thatched roofs, carved timber doorways and louvred shutters draw on traditional South Indian forms — set among lush tropical gardens, open terraces and a long lap pool. Rooms are spacious, simply furnished, and quiet.
